image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a collection of approximately 12-15 hockey pucks scattered on a neutral gray surface. The pucks are black vulcanized rubber disks with various colorful logos and text printed on their top faces. Some pucks show the side profile, revealing the characteristic ridged edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact solid disk with diameter moderately exceeding its thickness, creating a stout cylindrical profile.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All visible objects maintain the correct aspect ratio of a standard hockey puck (diameter > thickness). The cylindrical geometry is consistent across all instances.
The objects appear as solid, opaque disks with no structural anomalies or transparency issues.
The base material of all pucks is a consistent matte black, distinct from the glossy printed logos.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Raised ridges or grooves around circumference for stick handling.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Several pucks positioned on their sides (e.g., center-left, bottom-center) clearly display the vertical striations/ridges typical of hockey puck edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Printed league logos, brand markings, or game identification numbers on faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Every visible puck face features distinct, colorful graphics resembling team logos or commemorative designs.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dense hard material producing sharp sound when struck.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Acoustic properties cannot be verified visually.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy vulcanized rubber construction with substantial weight for its compact size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Weight and density are physical properties not directly verifiable from a static image, though visual solidity implies it.
The non-printed areas of the pucks show a uniform, low-specular reflection consistent with smooth rubber.
The objects are unmistakably identifiable as hockey pucks based on shape, color, and edge features.

artifact_observations.location: Logos on multiple pucks (e.g., top-right red logo, bottom-right white logo)
artifact_observations.reasoning: While the logos are stylistically coherent, the text within them is largely illegible or pseudo-text (gibberish), which is a common artifact in AI-generated images containing text. It mimics the look of text without forming readable words.
Slight bleeding or softness where the colorful ink meets the black rubber surface, lacking the crisp edge definition of real printed vinyl or paint on rubber.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific class identity and distinguish from similar circular objects.
To rigorously evaluate the legibility and correctness of the text within the logos, addressing the observed gibberish.
To check for merging artifacts between overlapping pucks and ensure clean separation from the background.
To assess general coherence, lighting consistency, and subtle texture realism.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of text within logos
Sharpness of the boundary between printed logos and rubber surface
Geometric consistency of puck thickness and diameter across all instances
Presence of any fusion artifacts where pucks overlap
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'text_gibberish' artifact. In real hockey pucks, logos are usually crisp and often contain readable team names or league marks. AI often generates 'logo-like' shapes with fake text. Determine if the illegibility is due to resolution/angle or genuine generation failure. Also, verify if the edge ridges are physically consistent on all side-view pucks.
